Krasne Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Vinnytsia Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Krasne's own founding predates its Jewish history considerably: according to Karaite folklore, the town was established in the 13th century by 40 Karaite families. Jews are first documented here only in 1648, when they fled to nearby Bar hoping to escape the Khmelnytsky massacres. The community later grew to an extraordinary 92 percent of the town's population by 1897 — among the highest concentrations recorded in this collection. Under Transnistria administration, 300 Jews deported from Bessarabia and Bukovina were sent to a ghetto established here, joined by more from the Skazinets camp in 1942; many of Krasne's Jews perished in the Holocaust.
